overall: The AG found the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law by deliberating when three members attended a Planning Board meeting or in the brief post-meeting exchange. It noted a date error in the Planning Board's notice and declined to review the Advisory Committee emails.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Capital Planning Committee deliberated outside a posted meeting when a quorum of its members attended a Planning Board meeting on December 10.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Committee did not deliberate and thus did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged three Committee members were huddled and deliberating together after the December 10 Planning Board meeting; the Committee said the brief talk was not Committee business.
allegations.key_passage: Absent evidence to the contrary, we credit a public body

allegations.summary: Not alleged against the Committee: the Planning Board's notice for its December 10 meeting listed the date as December 12th. The AG found the date error made the notice insufficient.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Open Meeting Law requires that a notice include the date of a meeting, rather than the day, the notice was insufficient.

allegations.summary: Complainant's emails between Advisory Committee members were cited; the AG declined to review allegations against the Advisory Committee because the complaint was filed only with the Capital Planning Committee.
allegations.key_passage: we decline to review allegations against the Advisory Committee.
